items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1959-12-09
items.q: Earl Humphrey, give me that trombone. Let me show you how to play a trombone. Earl handed me the trombone, you know.

ctx.x: Nice little band over there. Chattron trumpet.

They had a pretty fat band over there. Hudson got drunk one night. He seen them trombone players, you know, how bad they play and everything. And he seen a couple of them funerals there. That's where I got my kids. He come over there and told him, the fella said, give me that trombone now. Earl Humphrey, give me that trombone. Let me show you how to play a trombone. Earl handed me the trombone, you know. You talk about blasting. He went to blasting, making everything, you know, all out of key and everything. The…
I think you told me he said he was going to give up music, was it? When he said music's gone to hell after your-

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: I was waiting with Charlie Love, Joe Robichill, drummer for Marl.

ctx.x: Who did you play with? Who were you playing with?

And there I was, I was waiting with Charlie Love, Joe Robichill, drummer for Marl. I'm Shreveport, I forget his name. I don't know what I call him. Always call him Nose, that's all I remember his name. Can't think his name. And, Kim will wake with us a while, he was just starting up. Well, uh, now he came with him. Yeah. I think he was going to school at the time. I wish I was.
Who were, now what about trombone plays? What styles did you, did there any, were there any particular people you, uh, you thought were particularly good or anything?
